//: Each command is wrapped in an inline `sh -c` that puts a recent node on PATH before exec'ing. A GUI-launched tool inherits the PATH captured at login rather than the one nvm's shell hooks build, so `npm run dev` could otherwise run under whatever node was default at boot -- surfacing as rolldown importing `styleText` from `node:util` (added in 20.12), an error naming neither node nor the version it wanted.
//sandbox: The launcher sandbox refuses to exec files inside the repo (so this cannot live in scripts/) and refuses to READ them (so it cannot consult .nvmrc, which is the obvious source). ~/.nvm is outside the repo and readable, so the version comes from nvm's `default` alias instead. If that alias is missing the glob degrades to every installed version and the numeric sort takes the highest -- a weaker guarantee than .nvmrc, stated here so nobody reads this as honouring the repo pin. tests/lint/node-version.test.mjs and scripts/check-node-version.cjs remain the checks that enforce the pin.

configurations.name: kiwicv-dev
runtimeArgs: d="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}/versions/node"; a="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}/alias/default"; v=''; [ -r "$a" ] && v=$(tr -d 'v \t\n\r' < "$a"); b=$(ls -d "$d/v$v"* 2>/dev/null | sort -t. -k1,1n -k2,2n -k3,3n | tail -1); [ -x "$b/bin/node" ] && PATH="$b/bin:$PATH"; export PATH; exec npm run dev
